answer: Cryptographic delay functions resist Sybil attacks by requiring agents to solve non-parallelizable sequential equations for identity renewal. An attacker incurs the verifiable cost of dedicating continuous processor cycles and power per persona. Whether an agent trades jade, hedges yarrow yields, or runs a data mirror, compute cannot be multiplexed across identities. However, adversaries with custom application-specific chips achieve superior clock speeds, marginalizing standard devices.
